name: Tsilo13/opentable-scraper
what_it_holds: An update/adaptation of the classic OpenTable seated-diners scraper originally popularized in Stefan Jansen's 'Machine Learning for Trading' alternative-data chapter. Sibling scraper repos exist (Litigator98765/opentable-scraper, Abdullah-Shaheer/opentable-scraper — top-100-restaurants only, navshar1999/opentable_scraper) plus an Apify-hosted commercial version (bondvit/opentable-crawler-examples). Checked stefan-jansen/machine-learning-for-trading directly: current version of that repo's own alt-data chapter no longer includes an OpenTable module (cut in a later edition), so these smaller forks are now the only GitHub trace of that method.
why_useful: OpenTable year-over-year seated-diner counts by city/state are a well-known local-economic-activity/leisure-spend proxy; a working scraper (unrun, per rules) could extend or refresh what we already hold conceptually (item 6, consumer spend panels) with a city-level dining-out signal correlated with tourism intensity, distinct from card-spend panels.

name: earnings-vol-study
what_it_holds: Python event study of 639 earnings announcements across 54 large-cap US stocks, 2023-2026, built on free DoltHub options/price data. Committed CSVs in /data/: universe.csv (54 tickers), events.csv (earnings dates), event_panel.csv (full implied-vol/price/straddle panel, ~500-639 rows), events_enriched.csv, plus JSON result files (rq1/rq2/rq3, multiple-testing correction). Findings: IV rises ~7.6 vol pts pre-announcement and crushes ~7.3 pts post; implied move (~4.6% median) exceeds realized move (~3.7%), premium ratio 1.22x (p=0.041); pre-event IV is dominant crush-magnitude driver (R2=0.50). Includes data-quality audits, out-of-sample splits, placebo tests, unit tests.
why_useful: Directly on-theme: a recent (through 2026), reproducible earnings-implied-move / IV-crush dataset and methodology built entirely on free data (DoltHub). If ABNB is among the 54 tickers this gives a ready calibration for the 5 Nov 2026 options-implied move; even if not, the method + DoltHub data source is directly replicable for ABNB. Also flags DoltHub as a free options-data source worth checking separately (fills gap #17 earnings-implied-move estimators, complements the existing reverse-DCF market-implied-move work).
size_hint: ~600-row event panel + several supporting CSVs/JSON, 12 commits
duplicate_of_holding: Complements, does not duplicate, our existing Bloomberg options workbook and reverse-DCF market-implied model (those are ABNB-specific and licensed/pull-date-anchored; this is free, cross-sectional, and gives an independent method).
themes: Event-study and factor packages; earnings-surprise datasets; post-earnings-drift replication; Ken French factor loaders
why_all: Directly on-theme: a recent (through 2026), reproducible earnings-implied-move / IV-crush dataset and methodology built entirely on free data (DoltHub). name: prediction-market-analysis
what_it_holds: Framework + released dataset described as 'the largest publicly available dataset of Polymarket and Kalshi market and trade data'. Parquet-based storage: Kalshi/{markets,trades}, Polymarket/{blocks,markets,trades}. A pre-collected 36GB compressed archive (data.tar.zst) is offered via Cloudflare R2 download. MIT licensed, 3.8k stars/541 forks, 30 commits on main. Not filtered to any single event category — covers all Polymarket/Kalshi markets and trades, so earnings, macro, travel and regulation contracts (e.g. any 'will ABNB report X', CPI/travel-demand-adjacent markets, hurricane/weather markets) would be included wherever they were listed on either venue.
why_useful: Point-in-time market/trade-level data (order-level, timestamped) is exactly the kind of vintage series gap #4 calls for; could be filtered for ABNB-earnings contracts, travel-shock markets (hurricanes, World Cup 2026), or regulatory-event contracts (STR ordinances, FTC/DOJ actions) if such markets existed on Kalshi/Polymarket historically. Also usable as a general market-implied-probability cross-check for event studies (gap #11, #12).
time_coverage: Full available Polymarket/Kalshi trade history up to repo's collection date (exact start not confirmed from README excerpt)
size_hint: 36GB compressed (data.tar.zst); Parquet files, additional CSV/JSON/PNG/PDF analysis outputs

name: kovagent/shortkit
what_it_holds: Rust crate/tool bundling US short-sale volume and FINRA short-interest data as parquet files, with a nightly-refresh mechanism and no API keys required (per description). Repo is small (has CHANGELOG.md, .github workflow) so likely thin, but the described data product is exactly FINRA short interest by ticker over time.

name: Fama-French and Hou-Xue-Zhang Factors Replication
what_it_holds: Committed Factors_monthly.csv and Factor_sharpe_ratios.csv in /master: replicated Fama-French 6-factor and Hou-Xue-Zhang q-factor monthly series, 1971-2024 (per repo README, though authors note earlier years constrained by missing accounting data for q-factors). Built from CRSP/Compustat/CCM (WRDS) but output CSVs are committed and usable without WRDS access; also includes benchmark comparison files vs Ken French library and global-q.org.
why_useful: Extends what we already hold (plain Ken French 3/5-factor series) with q-factor model loadings and a longer monthly panel; useful as an alternative risk model for an ABNB earnings-day event study / CAR calculation, and a free cross-check against the Ken French numbers we already pull. Not a numbered gap but directly on-theme (Ken French factor loader + broader factor set).
duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our existing Ken French factors holding but adds q-factors and a committed CSV rather than a live pull
